source.text: Οὔσης οὖν ὀψίας τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ τῇ μιᾷ σαββάτων, καὶ τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων ὅπου ἦσαν οἱ μαθηταὶ διὰ τὸν φόβον τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἦλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἔστη εἰς τὸ μέσον, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Being therefore evening on the day that, the first of [the] week, and the doors having been shut where were the disciples because of the fear of the Jews, came the Jesus and stood into the middle, and says to them, "Peace to you."

en.L: So when it was evening on that day, the first [day] of the week, and the doors had been shut where the disciples were, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the middle and says to them, "Peace to you."
en.B: On the evening of that day, the first day of the week, the disciples were behind locked doors because they feared the Jewish leaders. Jesus came and stood among them and said, "Peace to you."
en.R: It was the evening of that same Sunday, the first day of the week. The disciples were together, and they had locked the doors because they were afraid of the Jewish leaders. Then Jesus came and stood among them. He said to them, "Peace be with you."

fr.L: Comme il était donc le soir, ce jour-là, le premier [jour] de la semaine, et que les portes avaient été fermées là où étaient les disciples, par crainte des Juifs, Jésus vint et se tint au milieu, et il leur dit : « Paix à vous. »
fr.B: Le soir de ce même jour, le premier jour de la semaine, les disciples se trouvaient derrière des portes verrouillées, parce qu’ils craignaient les chefs juifs. Jésus vint, se tint au milieu d’eux et leur dit : « Paix à vous. »
fr.R: C’était le soir de ce même dimanche, le premier jour de la semaine. Les disciples étaient ensemble, et ils avaient fermé les portes à clé, parce qu’ils avaient peur des chefs juifs. Alors Jésus est venu et il s’est tenu au milieu d’eux. Il leur a dit : « La paix soit avec vous. »

sw.L: Basi ikiwa ni jioni ya siku ile, ya kwanza ya juma, na milango ya mahali walipokuwa wanafunzi ikiwa imefungwa kwa sababu ya hofu ya Wayahudi, Yesu akaja, akasimama katikati, naye anawaambia, "Amani iwe nanyi."
sw.B: Jioni ya siku ile, siku ya kwanza ya juma, wanafunzi walikuwa ndani, milango imefungwa kwa kufuli, kwa sababu waliwaogopa viongozi wa Wayahudi. Yesu akaja, akasimama katikati yao, akasema, "Amani iwe nanyi."
sw.R: Ilikuwa jioni ya siku ile ile ya Jumapili, siku ya kwanza ya juma. Wanafunzi walikuwa pamoja, nao walikuwa wamefunga milango kwa kufuli kwa sababu waliwaogopa viongozi wa Wayahudi. Ndipo Yesu akaja, akasimama katikati yao. Akawaambia, "Amani iwe nanyi."

vi.L: Vậy, khi trời đã tối vào ngày ấy, ngày thứ nhất trong tuần, và các cửa đã đóng kín nơi các môn đồ đang ở, vì sợ người Do Thái, Đức Giê-xu đến, đứng ở giữa [họ] và nói với họ: "Bình an cho các con."
vi.B: Chiều tối hôm ấy, ngày thứ nhất trong tuần, các môn đồ đang ở trong nhà, cửa đóng kín vì sợ các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái. Đức Giê-xu đến, đứng giữa họ và nói: "Bình an cho các con."
vi.R: Chiều tối Chủ Nhật hôm ấy, tức là ngày thứ nhất trong tuần, các môn đồ đang họp lại với nhau. Họ đã khóa cửa vì sợ các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái. Lúc ấy Đức Giê-xu đến và đứng giữa họ. Ngài nói với họ: "Bình an ở cùng các con."

ko.L: 그러므로 그날, 곧 주간의 첫날 저녁이 되었을 때, 제자들이 있던 곳은 유대인들을 두려워하여 문들이 닫혀 있었는데, 예수께서 오셔서 가운데 서시고 그들에게 말씀하신다. "평안이 너희에게 [있기를]."
ko.B: 그날, 곧 주간의 첫날 저녁이었다. 제자들은 유대 지도자들이 두려워서 문을 걸어 잠그고 모여 있었다. 그때 예수께서 오셔서 그들 가운데 서시고 말씀하셨다. "너희에게 평안이 있기를 빈다."
ko.R: 바로 그날, 한 주의 첫날인 일요일 저녁이었다. 제자들은 한곳에 모여 있었는데, 유대 지도자들이 무서워서 문을 꼭 잠가 두었다. 그때 예수께서 오셔서 그들 가운데 서셨다. 그리고 말씀하셨다. "너희에게 평안이 있기를!"

decisions.choice: the Jews: the religious authorities in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The disciples fear the same authorities who had Jesus arrested and handed over to Pilate (18:3, 12; 19:7, 12-15), as people feared them before (7:13; 9:22; 19:38). It is not the people as a whole: the disciples themselves, and Jesus, are Jews.

decisions.choice: the evening of the same day, the first day of the week
alternatives: the start of the next day, counted from sunset
decisions.reason: "The first of the week" is the day the tomb was found empty (20:1), the day after the Sabbath. By Jewish reckoning a new day began at sunset, but John says it is still "that day": the risen Jesus meets his disciples on the day he rose.

decisions.choice: the doors had been shut and stayed shut
alternatives: the doors were being shut as he came
decisions.reason: The perfect participle describes a state: the doors were shut and remained so. John says that Jesus came and stood among them although the doors were shut (again in 20:26), but he does not say how he came in.

decisions.choice: Peace to you: the everyday greeting, now given its full weight
decisions.reason: "Peace" (shalom) was the ordinary Jewish greeting, a wish for wholeness and well-being from God. On Jesus's lips after his death and rising it is more than a greeting: it is the peace he promised to leave them (14:27; 16:33), now given.

decisions.choice: the Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: Where the word means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them (see the book's terms). The footnote gives the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal ("says", "comes"); past tense at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John, Literal keeps John's present tense ("says" in 20:19, 22, 27, 29; "comes" in 20:26), which makes the story vivid; Balanced and Readable use the past, as English tells a story. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: behind locked doors (B); locked, were together (R); Peace to you (L, B); Peace be with you (R)
decisions.reason: Doors shut out of fear were barred or bolted, so Balanced and Readable say "locked"; Literal keeps "shut". "Where the disciples were" implies they were in one place, which Balanced says with "behind locked doors" and Readable with "together". Readable uses the fuller form of the greeting that English speakers know; every level keeps "peace".

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John's present tense ("il dit", "Jésus vient"); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
the present tense throughout at Literal
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (20:19-31). The passé simple ("vint", "se tint") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Literal uses it for the Greek past tenses and keeps the present where John tells a past event in the present (20:19, 22, 27, 29 "il dit"; 20:26 "Jésus vient"), as the English Literal does. Readable uses the passé composé ("Jésus est venu"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first. Inside speech every level uses the passé composé ("nous avons vu", "tu as cru"), which in French serves for the Greek perfect as well as for a past event.

decisions.choice: les Juifs (L); les chefs juifs (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John, first used here in this passage. Literal keeps the word John wrote. Balanced and Readable name the group the context shows (meaning decision m1): in French, "les Juifs" alone reads as the whole people, while the disciples who are afraid are Jews themselves.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anawaambia here and in verses 22, 27 and 29; anakuja in verse 26); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As in 20:1-18: Literal keeps John's present tense for past events; Balanced tells the story in the narrative past with -li- and -ka-, and Readable uses the plain past. This holds for the whole of 20:19-31.

decisions.choice: Wayahudi (L); viongozi wa Wayahudi (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the book-wide choice for John: Literal keeps the word John wrote; Balanced and Readable name the authorities the disciples feared (meaning decision m1), so the text does not set the disciples, who were Jews, against the Jewish people. As in 7:13 and 9:22.

decisions.choice: Amani iwe nanyi (every level, here and in verses 21 and 26)
decisions.reason: The Greek greeting has no verb ("Peace to you"). Swahili says a wish of this kind with "iwe" (may it be), so the greeting reads naturally at every level and Literal needs no bracket; the English difference between "Peace to you" and "Peace be with you" does not arise.

decisions.choice: "các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái" (B, R); "người Do Thái" (L)
decisions.reason: The authorities are meant here (see the meaning decision); Literal keeps the word John wrote, as docs/john-terms.md sets for every language.

decisions.choice: "Bình an cho các con" (L, B); "Bình an ở cùng các con" (R); Jesus calls his disciples "các con"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must choose a relation in "you": Jesus speaks to his disciples as "các con" throughout the book (style guide section 6). "Bình an" keeps the key term rather than reducing the greeting to "chào".

decisions.choice: "유대인들" (L); "유대 지도자들" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As docs/john-terms.md: Literal shows the word John wrote; Balanced and Readable name the Jerusalem authorities whom the meaning decision identifies. The disciples are Jews themselves; what they fear is the authorities who had Jesus executed.

decisions.choice: historic present "말씀하신다", "오신다" (L); past tense (B, R), through 20:19-31
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present in narrative, which Korean can use for vividness; Balanced and Readable use the past. One decision for the passage.

decisions.choice: "평안" for eirēnē: "평안이 너희에게 [있기를]" (L); "너희에게 평안이 있기를 빈다" (B); "너희에게 평안이 있기를!" (R), the same at 20:21 and 20:26
alternatives: an everyday greeting such as "잘 있었느냐"
decisions.reason: "평안" is the book-wide key term for peace (style guide, section 6). The Greek is a verbless wish; Literal brackets the verb Korean needs, Balanced adds "빈다" (I wish) so the greeting reads as a blessing, and Readable keeps a short exclamation. An everyday Korean greeting would lose the weight the meaning decision gives it.

source.text: καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ἔδειξεν τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τὴν πλευρὰν αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And this having said he showed the hands and the side to them.

en.L: And having said this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed them [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] hands and [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] side.
en.B: After saying this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed them {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} side.
en.R: After saying this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} showed them the wounds in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} side.

fr.L: Et ayant dit cela, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur montra les mains et le côté.
fr.B: Après avoir dit cela, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur montra {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} mains et {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} côté.
fr.R: Après avoir dit cela, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a montré les blessures de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} mains et de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} côté.

sw.L: Na baada ya kusema hayo, aliwaonyesha mikono na ubavu.
sw.B: Baada ya kusema hivyo, aliwaonyesha mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na ubavu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Baada ya kusema hivyo, aliwaonyesha majeraha ya mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na ya ubavu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

vi.L: Và sau khi nói điều này, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho họ xem [đôi] tay và cạnh sườn [của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}].
vi.B: Nói xong, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho họ xem tay và sườn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Nói xong, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho họ xem những vết thương ở tay và ở sườn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 이것을 말씀하시고 나서, 그들에게 손과 옆구리를 보여 주셨다.
ko.B: 이렇게 말씀하신 뒤에, 예수께서 그들에게 두 손과 옆구리를 보여 주셨다.
ko.R: 이렇게 말씀하시고 나서, 예수께서는 두 손과 옆구리에 난 상처를 그들에게 보여 주셨다.

decisions.choice: the hands and side: the wounds of the cross, showing the risen one is the one crucified
alternatives: a proof only that he had a body
decisions.reason: His hands bore the marks of the nails (20:25) and his side the wound of the soldier's spear (19:34). By showing them, Jesus makes himself known: the one who stands among them is the same one who died. The wounds remain in his risen body (20:27).

decisions.choice: side: the side of the chest, where the spear went in
decisions.reason: The word is the one used in 19:34 of the spear wound, from which blood and water came out. Only John tells of it; in Luke 24:39-40 Jesus shows his hands and feet.

decisions.choice: [his] hands and [his] side (L); the wounds in his hands and his side (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "the hands and the side"; English needs "his", which Literal brackets. Readable names the wounds, which is what he showed (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: les mains et le côté (L)
alternatives: [ses] mains et [son] côté, as the English Literal
decisions.reason: French uses the definite article for parts of the body when it is clear whose they are ("il leur montra les mains"), so Literal follows the Greek and needs no bracketed possessive, unlike the English. Balanced says "ses mains et son côté", and Readable names the wounds (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, ubavu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} (B, R); mikono na ubavu (L)
decisions.reason: The deity_pronoun setting goes only on free pronouns and possessives; a subject or object prefix (aliwaonyesha) cannot take a capital, so Swahili has fewer spans than English throughout the passage. The Greek has no "his" here, and Swahili reads naturally without it, so Literal needs no bracket.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} for Jesus in the narrative
decisions.reason: The style guide's respectful narrative pronoun for Jesus; the setting changes only its capital. A pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly as "Ngài".

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean ("께서", the honorific -시-, "그분"), through 20:19-31
alternatives: deity_pronoun spans as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change (style guide, section 7); respect for Jesus is carried by "께서", the honorific -시- and "그분" at every level. Recorded once for this passage.

source.text: ἐχάρησαν οὖν οἱ μαθηταὶ ἰδόντες τὸν κύριον.

records.literal_gloss: Rejoiced therefore the disciples having seen the Lord.

en.L: So the disciples rejoiced, having seen the Lord.
en.B: Then the disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord.
en.R: The disciples were full of joy when they saw the Lord.

fr.L: Les disciples se réjouirent donc, ayant vu le Seigneur.
fr.B: Les disciples se réjouirent alors en voyant le Seigneur.
fr.R: Les disciples ont été remplis de joie quand ils ont vu le Seigneur.

sw.L: Basi wanafunzi walifurahi, kwa kuwa walimwona Bwana.

vi.L: Vậy các môn đồ vui mừng, khi đã thấy Chúa.
vi.B: Các môn đồ vui mừng khi thấy Chúa.
vi.R: Các môn đồ thấy Chúa thì rất vui mừng.

decisions.choice: the joy Jesus promised: "I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice"
decisions.reason: In 16:20-22 Jesus told them that their grief would turn to joy when they saw him again, and that no one would take that joy from them. John uses the same verb for rejoice here: the promise is kept.

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus, now known as the risen Lord
alternatives: sir or master, an address of respect
decisions.reason: The narrator calls Jesus "the Lord" here, as Mary Magdalene has just done (20:18, "I have seen the Lord") and the disciples will say to Thomas (20:25). The title points toward Thomas's confession, "My Lord and my God" (20:28).

decisions.choice: they rejoiced because they saw him
alternatives: they rejoiced, and also saw him
decisions.reason: The word "therefore" and the participle "having seen" tie the joy to the sight: they rejoiced when, and because, they saw the Lord.

decisions.choice: were full of joy
decisions.reason: Readable uses the noun "joy", the plainer expression, which also keeps the link with Jesus's promise of joy in 16:20-22.

decisions.choice: "뵙고" (B, R) for "having seen"; "보고" (L)
decisions.reason: "뵙다" is the humble verb for seeing someone honoured, which is how the disciples now see the risen Lord; Literal keeps the plain verb of the Greek.

source.text: εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν· Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν· καθὼς ἀπέσταλκέν με ὁ πατήρ, κἀγὼ πέμπω ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: Said therefore to them the Jesus again, "Peace to you; just as has sent me the Father, I also send you."

en.L: So Jesus said to them again, "Peace to you. Just as the Father has sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I also send you."
en.B: Jesus said to them again, "Peace to you. In the way that the Father has sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I am sending you."
en.R: Again Jesus said to them, "Peace be with you. The Father has sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. In the same way, I am sending you."

fr.L: Jésus leur dit donc de nouveau : « Paix à vous. Comme le Père {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aussi je vous envoie. »
fr.B: Jésus leur dit de nouveau : « Paix à vous. De même que le Père {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aussi, je vous envoie. »
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit encore : « La paix soit avec vous. Le Père {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé. De la même façon, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je vous envoie. »

sw.L: Basi Yesu akawaambia tena, "Amani iwe nanyi. Kama vile Baba amenituma, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} pia ninawatuma ninyi."
sw.B: Yesu akawaambia tena, "Amani iwe nanyi. Kwa jinsi ileile Baba alivyonituma, ndivyo {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninavyowatuma ninyi."
sw.R: Yesu akawaambia tena, "Amani iwe nanyi. Baba amenituma. Vivyo hivyo, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninawatuma ninyi."

vi.L: Vậy Đức Giê-xu lại nói với họ: "Bình an cho các con. Như Cha đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sai các con."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu lại nói với họ: "Bình an cho các con. Như Cha đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đi, nay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sai các con đi."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu lại nói với họ: "Bình an ở cùng các con. Cha đã sai {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đến. Bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sai các con đi như vậy."

ko.L: 그러므로 예수께서 다시 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "평안이 너희에게 [있기를]. 아버지께서 나를 보내신 것처럼, 나도 너희를 보낸다."
ko.B: 예수께서 다시 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희에게 평안이 있기를 빈다. 아버지께서 나를 보내셨듯이, 이제 나도 너희를 보낸다."
ko.R: 예수께서 다시 말씀하셨다. "너희에게 평안이 있기를! 아버지께서 나를 보내셨다. 그와 똑같이 나도 너희를 보낸다."

decisions.choice: has sent, send: two Greek verbs with the same meaning here
alternatives: a difference in meaning between the two verbs, such as an official commission for the first
decisions.reason: John uses both verbs, ἀπέσταλκέν and πέμπω, of the Father sending the Son (for example 3:17 and 5:23-24), and both of Jesus sending others (4:38; 13:20). Here they most likely vary for style, and the point is that the sendings match. Because the first verb is related to the word "apostle", some take it to stress an official commission, but John uses the two freely.

decisions.choice: the Father has sent: a sending that still stands; I send: now
decisions.reason: The first verb is perfect: the Father sent Jesus and he remains the one sent. The second is present: Jesus is sending them now, as he said he would in his prayer (17:18).

decisions.choice: the disciples' mission is patterned on Jesus's own
alternatives: a separate mission of their own
decisions.reason: Jesus is "the one sent" throughout John (3:17; 5:36; 17:3, 8). Now the disciples share his mission in the world, as 13:20 and 17:18 foretold. What follows, the gift of the Spirit and the word about forgiving sins (20:22-23), belongs to this sending.

decisions.choice: Peace to you again: a second greeting that opens the commissioning
decisions.reason: Jesus has already greeted them (20:19). Saying it again marks a new start: having shown them his wounds, he now sends them out, and he sends them with his peace (14:27).

decisions.choice: In the way that ... I am sending you (B); The Father has sent me. In the same way, I am sending you. (R)
alternatives: As the Father has sent me, so I send you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out that the two sendings match (meaning decision m3), with wording like 17:18; the English present "am sending" fits a sending that happens now (m2). Readable keeps "Peace be with you" as in 20:19.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:m'|M'}}a envoyé ... {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aussi, je vous envoie
alternatives: je vous envoie à mon tour
je suis en train de vous envoyer
decisions.reason: The French present "je vous envoie" says both "I send" and "I am sending", so it carries the sending that happens now (meaning decision m2) without the heavy "être en train de"; the passé composé "m'a envoyé" keeps the lasting result of the Greek perfect. The stressed "moi" renders the "I also" of the Greek and, being Jesus speaking of himself, takes the deity_pronoun setting. Both verbs are "envoyer", as the English uses "send" for both (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: kutuma for both verbs (amenituma, ninawatuma)
decisions.reason: John uses two Greek verbs for "send" here with the same meaning (meaning decision m1), and the point is that the two sendings match. Swahili uses one verb for both, which shows that match; the perfect "amenituma" and the present "ninawatuma" keep the tenses (m2).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} for Jesus speaking of himself
decisions.reason: The style guide's form for Jesus's "I" throughout John; the setting changes only the capital. Paired with "các con" for the disciples.

source.text: καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ἐνεφύσησεν καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Λάβετε πνεῦμα ἅγιον·

records.literal_gloss: And this having said he breathed on and says to them, "Receive Holy Spirit."

en.L: And having said this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} breathed on [them] and says to them, "Receive [the] Holy Spirit."
en.B: Having said this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} breathed on them and told them, "Receive the Holy Spirit."
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} breathed on them. He said, "Receive the Holy Spirit."

fr.L: Et ayant dit cela, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} souffla [sur eux] et leur dit : « Recevez [l’]Esprit Saint. »
fr.B: Après avoir dit cela, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} souffla sur eux et leur dit : « Recevez l’Esprit Saint. »
fr.R: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a soufflé sur eux. Il leur a dit : « Recevez l’Esprit Saint. »

sw.L: Na alipokwisha kusema hayo, akawapumulia, naye anawaambia, "Pokeeni Roho Mtakatifu."
sw.B: Baada ya kusema hayo, akawapumulia, akawaambia, "Pokeeni Roho Mtakatifu."

vi.L: Và sau khi nói điều này, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thổi hơi [trên họ] và nói với họ: "Hãy nhận Đức Thánh Linh."
vi.B: Nói xong, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thổi hơi trên họ và bảo: "Hãy nhận lấy Đức Thánh Linh."
vi.R: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thổi hơi trên họ. Ngài nói: "Hãy nhận lấy Đức Thánh Linh."

ko.L: 그리고 이것을 말씀하시고 나서 [그들에게] 숨을 내쉬시고, 그들에게 말씀하신다. "성령을 받아라."
ko.B: 이 말씀을 하시고 나서 그들에게 숨을 불어넣으시며 말씀하셨다. "성령을 받아라."
ko.R: 그리고 예수께서 그들을 향해 숨을 내쉬시며 말씀하셨다. "성령을 받아라."

decisions.choice: he breathed on them: echoing God breathing life into the first man
alternatives: an ordinary gesture with no echo intended
decisions.reason: The verb ἐνεφύσησεν is rare. The same form is used in the Greek Old Testament of God breathing the breath of life into the man he had formed (Genesis 2:7), and the verb is used when the breath of God gives life to the dead bones (Ezekiel 37:9). The echo suggests a new creation: the risen Jesus gives new life by his Spirit (compare 3:5-8). The text does not say this in so many words.

decisions.choice: Receive the Holy Spirit: Jesus gives the Spirit he promised, now that he is glorified
alternatives: only a promise of a later gift
a different gift from the Spirit poured out at Pentecost
decisions.reason: Jesus had said that the Spirit would be given once he was glorified (7:39) and that he would send the Advocate when he went away (14:16-17, 26; 15:26; 16:7). Here he gives the Spirit with a word and a gesture. John does not say how this relates to the coming of the Spirit at Pentecost (Acts 2:1-4). It may be John's account of the same gift, a first giving followed by a fuller one, or a sign of what was to come; the text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: Holy Spirit without the article: God's Spirit, not a mere influence
alternatives: a gift or power of the Spirit, as distinct from the Spirit himself
decisions.reason: Greek often leaves out the article with "Holy Spirit" (as in 1:33). Some take the lack of the article to mean a gift from the Spirit, but in this setting, after the promises of chapters 14-16, it is the Holy Spirit himself who is given. So the word has a capital S.

decisions.choice: breathed on [them]; Receive [the] Holy Spirit (L); them, the (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb has no object, but those he breathed on are the disciples he is speaking to. English needs "the" before "Holy Spirit" (meaning decision m3). Literal brackets both.

decisions.choice: souffla [sur eux]; [l']Esprit Saint
decisions.reason: French "souffler" without an object would mean only that he breathed out, and French cannot say "Recevez Esprit Saint", so Literal brackets both, as "[l']Esprit Saint" in 1:33 (meaning decision m3). "L'Esprit Saint" is the form used throughout John in French.

decisions.choice: akawapumulia (breathed on them)
decisions.reason: "Kupumua" is the verb for breathing, so it keeps the echo of God breathing the breath of life into the first man (meaning decision m1); "kupuliza" is blowing, as on a fire. The object prefix -wa- says "on them" inside the verb, so Literal needs no bracket where the English has "[them]". Swahili has no article, so "Roho Mtakatifu" needs none either (m3).

decisions.choice: "thổi hơi trên họ"
decisions.reason: Plain modern verb for breathing on someone; "hà hơi" is the older wording readers may remember.

decisions.choice: "숨을 불어넣으시며" (B); "숨을 내쉬시고" (L, R)
decisions.reason: "불어넣다" (breathe into) is the Korean phrase for God breathing life into the first man, so Balanced lets the echo the meaning decision notes be heard; Literal and Readable keep the plain act of breathing out. Korean has no article, so "성령" needs no bracket at Literal.

source.text: ἄν τινων ἀφῆτε τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἀφέωνται αὐτοῖς· ἄν τινων κρατῆτε κεκράτηνται.

records.literal_gloss: If of any you forgive the sins, they have been forgiven to them; if of any you retain, they have been retained.

en.L: If you forgive the sins of any, they have been forgiven them; if you retain [the sins] of any, they have been retained.
en.B: Whose sins you forgive, they stand forgiven; whose sins you retain, they stand retained.
en.R: When you forgive people's sins, those sins are forgiven. When you hold people's sins against them, those sins remain.

fr.L: Si vous remettez les péchés de certains, ils leur ont été remis ; si vous retenez [ceux] de certains, ils ont été retenus.
fr.B: Si vous remettez à quelqu’un ses péchés, ils lui sont remis ; si vous les lui retenez, ils lui restent retenus.
fr.R: Quand vous pardonnez aux gens leurs péchés, ces péchés sont pardonnés. Quand vous ne les leur pardonnez pas, ces péchés leur restent attachés.

sw.L: Mkiwasamehe watu wowote dhambi zao, zimesamehewa; mkiwashikilia watu wowote [dhambi zao], zimeshikiliwa.
sw.B: Wale mtakaowasamehe dhambi zao, wamesamehewa; wale mtakaowashikilia dhambi zao, dhambi hizo zinabaki zimeshikiliwa.
sw.R: Mkiwasamehe watu dhambi zao, dhambi hizo zimesamehewa. Mkiwahesabia watu dhambi zao, dhambi hizo zinabaki juu yao.

vi.L: Nếu các con tha tội cho người nào, thì tội họ đã được tha; nếu các con giữ lại [tội] của người nào, thì [tội ấy] đã bị giữ lại.
vi.B: Các con tha tội cho ai thì tội người ấy được tha; các con giữ tội ai lại thì tội người ấy vẫn bị giữ lại.
vi.R: Khi các con tha tội cho người nào, tội của người đó được tha. Khi các con không tha mà giữ tội người nào lại, tội của người đó vẫn còn.

ko.L: 너희가 누구의 죄든지 용서하면 그들에게 [그 죄가] 용서된 것이고, 누구의 [죄든지] 붙잡아 두면 [그 죄는] 붙잡혀 있는 것이다.
ko.B: 너희가 용서하는 사람의 죄는 이미 용서된 것이고, 너희가 붙들어 두는 사람의 죄는 그대로 붙들려 있는 것이다.
ko.R: 너희가 사람들의 죄를 용서하면 그 죄는 용서받는다. 너희가 사람들의 죄를 용서하지 않고 그대로 두면 그 죄는 그대로 남는다.

decisions.choice: an authority given to the disciples as a community sent by Jesus
alternatives: an authority given to particular leaders only
a power to forgive apart from God
decisions.reason: The verbs are plural: Jesus speaks to the disciples gathered in the room (20:19), who are sent as he was sent and have received the Spirit (20:21-22). The forgiving of sins belongs to that mission. The text does not say how it is to be carried out. Later churches applied it in different ways: some to the forgiveness pronounced by ordained ministers, others to the preaching of the gospel and the discipline of the whole church. The words themselves do not decide between these.

decisions.choice: they have been forgiven, they have been retained: a result that stands, with God as the one who forgives
alternatives: the disciples forgive in their own right
decisions.reason: Both verbs are perfect passives. The passive leaves the one who forgives unnamed; in the Bible only God forgives sins in the end (Mark 2:7). The perfect says the result stands. Whether it means that God has already forgiven what they declare forgiven, or that he confirms what they do, is debated; the tense alone does not settle it.

decisions.choice: forgive and retain: release and hold fast
decisions.reason: The verb for "forgive" means to let go or release; the verb for "retain", κρατῆτε, means to hold on to or keep hold of. Sins are either released from people or kept bound to them. Compare "bind" and "loose" in Matthew 16:19 and 18:18.

decisions.choice: Whose sins ... they stand forgiven ... stand retained (B); hold people's sins against them ... remain (R)
alternatives: they are forgiven ... they are retained
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "stand" for the perfect tense, a result that holds (meaning decision m2). Readable puts "retain" into plain words, holding a wrong against someone, and says the sins remain, which is the opposite of forgiven (m3). "People" and "whose" include men and women.

decisions.choice: remettre ... retenir (L, B); pardonner ... leur restent attachés (R)
decisions.reason: The two verbs are "release" and "hold fast" (meaning decision m3). French "remettre" is to release someone from a debt or a sin, and it pairs with "retenir", to keep hold of, so Literal and Balanced keep the pair. Readable uses the everyday "pardonner" and says the sins "leur restent attachés", which keeps the picture of sins held to a person. Literal keeps the Greek perfect passive with "ont été remis"; Balanced's present passive "sont remis", "restent retenus" states a result that holds (m2) without naming who forgives. "Quelqu'un" and "les gens" include men and women.

decisions.choice: kusamehe ... kushikilia (L, B); kusamehe ... kuwahesabia (R)
decisions.reason: The verb for "retain" means to hold fast, the opposite of releasing (meaning decision m3), which "kushikilia" says. "Kufungia" (bind) would bring in the image of binding and loosing from Matthew 16:19, which this verse does not use. Readable says "kuwahesabia dhambi", to count sins against people. Balanced says the result stands with the perfect and "zinabaki" (m2).

decisions.choice: "giữ lại" for kratein (retain)
decisions.reason: Modern and literal ("hold fast"); Readable adds "không tha mà" so new readers see that retaining is the opposite of forgiving.

decisions.choice: "붙잡아 두다" (L); "붙들어 두다" (B); "용서하지 않고 그대로 두다" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb means to hold fast, the opposite of releasing; "붙잡아 두다" / "붙들어 두다" keep that picture and its pairing with the perfect passive ("붙잡혀 있는 것이다"). Readable says plainly what holding sins means.

source.text: Θωμᾶς δὲ εἷς ἐκ τῶν δώδεκα, ὁ λεγόμενος Δίδυμος, οὐκ ἦν μετ’ αὐτῶν ὅτε ἦλθεν Ἰησοῦς.

records.literal_gloss: Thomas but, one of the Twelve, the [one] called Didymus, not was with them when came Jesus.

en.L: But Thomas, one of the Twelve, the [one] called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.
en.B: But Thomas, one of the Twelve, also called Didymus (which means Twin), was not with them when Jesus came.
en.R: But Thomas was not with them when Jesus came. He was one of the twelve disciples, and he was called the Twin.

fr.L: Mais Thomas, l’un des Douze, [celui] appelé Didyme, n’était pas avec eux quand Jésus vint.
fr.B: Mais Thomas, l’un des Douze, appelé Didyme (ce qui veut dire Jumeau), n’était pas avec eux quand Jésus vint.
fr.R: Mais Thomas n’était pas avec eux quand Jésus est venu. C’était l’un des douze disciples, et on l’appelait le Jumeau.

sw.L: Lakini Tomaso, mmoja wa wale Kumi na Wawili, aitwaye Didimo, hakuwa pamoja nao Yesu alipokuja.
sw.B: Lakini Tomaso, mmoja wa wale Kumi na Wawili, aitwaye pia Didimo (maana yake Pacha), hakuwa pamoja nao Yesu alipokuja.
sw.R: Lakini Tomaso hakuwa pamoja nao Yesu alipokuja. Yeye alikuwa mmoja wa wale wanafunzi kumi na wawili, na aliitwa Pacha.

vi.L: Nhưng Thô-ma, một trong Mười Hai [người], người được gọi là Đi-đim, đã không ở với họ khi Đức Giê-xu đến.
vi.B: Nhưng Thô-ma, một người trong nhóm Mười Hai, cũng gọi là Đi-đim (nghĩa là "Sinh Đôi"), không có mặt với họ khi Đức Giê-xu đến.
vi.R: Nhưng lúc Đức Giê-xu đến, Thô-ma không có mặt với họ. Ông là một trong mười hai môn đồ, và người ta gọi ông là Sinh Đôi.

ko.L: 그러나 열둘 가운데 하나로서 디두모라고 불리는 도마는 예수께서 오셨을 때 그들과 함께 있지 않았다.
ko.B: 그러나 열두 제자 가운데 하나인 도마, 곧 쌍둥이라는 뜻의 디두모라고도 불리는 도마는 예수께서 오셨을 때 그들과 함께 있지 않았다.
ko.R: 그런데 예수께서 오셨을 때 도마는 그 자리에 없었다. 도마는 열두 제자 가운데 한 사람이었고, 쌍둥이라고 불렸다.

decisions.choice: Thomas called Didymus: both names mean "twin"
decisions.reason: As in 11:16, John gives the Greek word for Thomas's Semitic name, which means "twin". Whose twin he was is never said.

decisions.choice: the Twelve: the inner group Jesus chose
decisions.reason: "The Twelve" are the disciples Jesus chose (6:67-71). John notes that Thomas belongs to them, so his absence leaves one of the chosen witnesses without the experience the others had. The group in 20:19 is called simply "the disciples" and may have included others besides the Twelve.

decisions.choice: Didymus (which means Twin) (B); the twelve disciples, the Twin (R)
decisions.reason: As at 11:16, Balanced adds the meaning of the name and Readable gives only the meaning. Readable says "the twelve disciples" for the title "the Twelve" and splits the sentence.

decisions.choice: "Đi-đim (nghĩa là "Sinh Đôi")" (B); "Sinh Đôi" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek name means "twin"; Balanced explains it, Readable uses the meaning as the nickname.

decisions.choice: "열둘" (L); "열두 제자" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Korean "열둘" alone is only a number and does not read as the name of a group; Balanced and Readable add "제자" so the Twelve are recognised. Literal keeps the Greek's bare numeral.

source.text: ἔλεγον οὖν αὐτῷ οἱ ἄλλοι μαθηταί· Ἑωράκαμεν τὸν κύριον.

records.literal_gloss: Were saying therefore to him the other disciples, "We have seen the Lord."

en.L: So the other disciples were saying to him, "We have seen the Lord."
en.B: So the other disciples kept telling him, "We have seen the Lord!"
en.R: The other disciples told him again and again, "We have seen the Lord!"

fr.L: Les autres disciples lui disaient donc : « Nous avons vu le Seigneur. »
fr.B: Les autres disciples ne cessaient de lui dire : « Nous avons vu le Seigneur ! »
fr.R: Les autres disciples lui ont répété plusieurs fois : « Nous avons vu le Seigneur ! »

sw.L: Basi wale wanafunzi wengine walikuwa wakimwambia, "Tumemwona Bwana."
sw.B: Basi wanafunzi wengine wakaendelea kumwambia, "Tumemwona Bwana!"
sw.R: Wanafunzi wengine walimwambia tena na tena, "Tumemwona Bwana!"

vi.L: Vậy các môn đồ khác nói với ông: "Chúng tôi đã thấy Chúa."
vi.B: Các môn đồ khác cứ nói với ông: "Chúng tôi đã thấy Chúa!"
vi.R: Các môn đồ khác nói đi nói lại với ông: "Chúng tôi đã thấy Chúa!"

ko.L: 그러므로 다른 제자들이 그에게 말하고 있었다. "우리가 주님을 보았다."
ko.B: 그래서 다른 제자들이 그에게 거듭 말했다. "우리가 주님을 보았다!"
ko.R: 다른 제자들이 도마에게 몇 번이고 말했다. "우리가 주님을 보았다!"

decisions.choice: were saying: telling him more than once
decisions.reason: The verb is imperfect, which can describe an action repeated or kept up. They went on telling him, and he went on refusing.

decisions.choice: We have seen the Lord: the same witness Mary Magdalene gave
decisions.reason: Mary told the disciples, "I have seen the Lord" (20:18), with the same verb in the same tense. Now the disciples give that witness to Thomas. The perfect tense speaks of a seeing whose effect lasts.

decisions.choice: kept telling (B); told him again and again (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the repeated telling (meaning decision m1). The exclamation mark shows their excitement, which the setting implies.

decisions.choice: disaient (L)
decisions.reason: The French imperfect, like the Greek one, describes an action kept up or repeated (meaning decision m1), so Literal can say "disaient" where the English Literal needs "were saying". Balanced and Readable make the repetition explicit.

decisions.choice: "ông" for Thomas in the narrative; the disciples say "chúng tôi" among themselves
decisions.reason: Narrator refers to the disciples as "ông", the usual respectful form for a grown man; "chúng tôi" because Thomas, who did not see, is not included in "we".

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐὰν μὴ ἴδω ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν αὐτοῦ τὸν τύπον τῶν ἥλων καὶ βάλω τὸν δάκτυλόν μου εἰς τὸν τύπον τῶν ἥλων καὶ βάλω μου τὴν χεῖρα εἰς τὴν πλευρὰν αὐτοῦ, οὐ μὴ πιστεύσω.

records.literal_gloss: He but said to them, "If not I see in the hands of him the imprint of the nails and put the finger of me into the imprint of the nails and put of me the hand into the side of him, not not I will believe."

en.L: But he said to them, "If I do not see in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands the imprint of the nails, and put my finger into the imprint of the nails, and put my hand into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} side, I will certainly not believe."
en.B: But he told them, "I will never believe it unless I see the marks the nails made in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands, and put my finger into those marks, and put my hand into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} side."
en.R: But Thomas said, "First I must see the marks of the nails in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands. I must put my finger into those marks and put my hand into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} side. If I do not, I will never believe."

fr.L: Mais lui leur dit : « Si je ne vois pas dans {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} mains l’empreinte des clous, et ne mets pas mon doigt dans l’empreinte des clous, et ne mets pas ma main dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} côté, non, je ne croirai pas. »
fr.B: Mais il leur dit : « Je n’y croirai jamais, à moins de voir dans {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} mains la marque des clous, de mettre mon doigt dans ces marques et de mettre ma main dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} côté. »
fr.R: Mais Thomas a dit : « D’abord, il faut que je voie la marque des clous dans {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} mains. Il faut que je mette mon doigt dans ces marques et ma main dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} côté. Sinon, je ne croirai jamais. »

sw.L: Lakini yeye akawaambia, "Nisipoona katika mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} chapa ya misumari, na kutia kidole changu katika chapa ya misumari, na kutia mkono wangu katika ubavu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, hakika sitaamini."
sw.B: Lakini yeye akawaambia, "Sitaamini kamwe mpaka nione alama zilizoachwa na misumari katika mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, na kutia kidole changu katika alama hizo, na kutia mkono wangu katika ubavu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}."
sw.R: Lakini Tomaso akasema, "Kwanza lazima nione alama za misumari katika mikono {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Lazima nitie kidole changu katika alama hizo, na kutia mkono wangu katika ubavu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Nisipofanya hivyo, sitaamini kamwe."

vi.L: Nhưng ông nói với họ: "Nếu tôi không thấy dấu đinh trong tay Thầy, và không đặt ngón tay tôi vào dấu đinh, và không đặt bàn tay tôi vào sườn Thầy, thì tôi nhất định không tin."
vi.B: Nhưng ông bảo họ: "Tôi sẽ không bao giờ tin, trừ khi tôi thấy dấu đinh trên tay Thầy, đặt ngón tay vào dấu đinh ấy và đặt bàn tay vào sườn Thầy."
vi.R: Nhưng Thô-ma nói: "Trước hết tôi phải thấy dấu đinh trên tay Thầy. Tôi phải đặt ngón tay vào những dấu đinh đó và đặt bàn tay vào sườn Thầy. Nếu không, tôi sẽ không bao giờ tin."

ko.L: 그러나 그는 그들에게 말했다. "내가 그분의 손에서 못 자국을 보고, 내 손가락을 그 못 자국에 넣고, 내 손을 그분의 옆구리에 넣지 않으면, 나는 결코 믿지 않겠다."
ko.B: 그러나 도마는 그들에게 말했다. "나는 그분의 두 손에 난 못 자국을 직접 보고, 그 못 자국에 내 손가락을 넣어 보고, 그분의 옆구리에 내 손을 넣어 보지 않고서는 절대로 믿지 않겠다."
ko.R: 그러나 도마는 이렇게 말했다. "먼저 그분의 손에 있는 못 자국을 내 눈으로 봐야겠다. 그 못 자국에 내 손가락을 넣어 보고, 그분의 옆구리에 내 손을 넣어 봐야겠다. 그렇게 하지 않으면 나는 절대로 믿지 않겠다."

decisions.choice: I will certainly not believe: the strongest denial in Greek
alternatives: I will not believe (a plain refusal)
decisions.reason: Two negatives together, "not" and "not", make the firmest possible denial. Thomas asks to see what the others saw (20:20) and to touch it as well.

decisions.choice: imprint: the mark left by the nails
decisions.reason: The word means the mark struck or pressed into something, such as the impression of a seal. Here it is the wound the nails left.

decisions.choice: nails: Jesus was nailed to the cross
decisions.reason: The Romans sometimes tied a condemned person to the cross and sometimes nailed them. This is the only place in the Gospels that mentions nails in Jesus's crucifixion (compare Luke 24:39; Colossians 2:14). The word for "hand" can include the wrist.

decisions.choice: I will never believe it unless ... (B); First I must ... If I do not, I will never believe. (R)
alternatives: Unless I see ..., I will never believe (Greek order)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the refusal first, which is natural English for a long condition; Readable breaks the conditions into short sentences and names Thomas as the speaker. Literal keeps the Greek order.

decisions.choice: l'empreinte des clous (L); la marque des clous (B, R); non, je ne croirai pas (L); jamais (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Empreinte" is the mark pressed into something, as a seal leaves it (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable say "marque", the everyday word. French has no double negative to match the Greek "not not" (m1), so Literal puts a stressed "non" before the denial and the other levels say "jamais".

decisions.choice: chapa ya misumari (L); alama za misumari (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal uses "chapa", a mark stamped or pressed in, like the impression of a seal, which is what the Greek word means (meaning decision m2). Balanced and Readable use the everyday "alama" (mark).

decisions.choice: "Thầy" for "his" (Jesus) in Thomas's words
decisions.reason: A disciple speaking of Jesus to the other disciples uses the noun of address "Thầy" (style guide section 6); it is required by Vietnamese respect and is not bracketed at Literal.

decisions.choice: the disciples speak among themselves in 해라체, and Thomas calls Jesus "그분"
decisions.reason: The disciples are equals, so the plain style suits them (style guide, section 4); "그분" keeps Thomas's respect for the Jesus he cannot yet believe has risen.

source.text: Καὶ μεθ’ ἡμέρας ὀκτὼ πάλιν ἦσαν ἔσω οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ Θωμᾶς μετ’ αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And after days eight again were inside the disciples of him and Thomas with them.

en.L: And after eight days {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were again inside, and Thomas [was] with them.
en.B: A week later {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were indoors again, and Thomas was with them.
en.R: A week later, on the next Sunday, Jesus's disciples were together inside again. This time Thomas was with them.

fr.L: Et après huit jours, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples étaient de nouveau à l’intérieur, et Thomas [était] avec eux.
fr.B: Huit jours plus tard, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples étaient de nouveau à l’intérieur, et Thomas était avec eux.
fr.R: Une semaine plus tard, le dimanche suivant, les disciples de Jésus étaient de nouveau ensemble à l’intérieur. Cette fois, Thomas était avec eux.

sw.L: Na siku nane baadaye, wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa ndani tena, na Tomaso [alikuwa] pamoja nao.
sw.B: Juma moja baadaye wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa tena ndani ya nyumba, na Tomaso alikuwa pamoja nao.
sw.R: Juma moja baadaye, Jumapili iliyofuata, wanafunzi wa Yesu walikuwa tena pamoja ndani ya nyumba. Safari hii Tomaso alikuwa pamoja nao.

vi.L: Và sau tám ngày, các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại ở bên trong, và Thô-ma [ở] với họ.
vi.B: Một tuần sau, các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại ở trong nhà, và Thô-ma cũng ở với họ.
vi.R: Một tuần sau, vào Chủ Nhật kế tiếp, các môn đồ của Đức Giê-xu lại họp nhau trong nhà. Lần này Thô-ma có mặt với họ.

ko.L: 그리고 여드레 뒤에 그분의 제자들이 다시 안에 있었고, 도마도 그들과 함께 [있었다].
ko.B: 한 주일 뒤에 예수의 제자들이 다시 집 안에 모여 있었는데, 도마도 그들과 함께 있었다.
ko.R: 한 주가 지나 다음 일요일이 되었다. 예수의 제자들이 다시 집 안에 모여 있었다. 이번에는 도마도 함께 있었다.

decisions.choice: after eight days: a week later, on the next first day of the week
decisions.reason: Days were counted inclusively, so the first day and the last are both counted. "After eight days" means the same day the next week, that is, again the first day of the week (20:19).

decisions.choice: again inside: in the same place as before
decisions.reason: "Again" and "inside" point back to the scene of 20:19: the disciples are gathered behind shut doors once more. The difference is that Thomas is now there.

decisions.choice: A week later (B, R); on the next Sunday (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom (meaning decision m1). Readable names the day as in 20:19 and names Jesus, whom the Greek refers to as "his".

decisions.choice: après huit jours (L); huit jours plus tard (B); une semaine plus tard, le dimanche suivant (R)
alternatives: une semaine plus tard (B), as the English Balanced
decisions.reason: French still counts a week inclusively as "huit jours" ("dans huit jours", "lundi en huit"), so Balanced can keep John's number and still be read as "a week later", the same day of the next week (meaning decision m1). Readable says "une semaine" and names the day, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "여드레 뒤에" (L); "한 주일 뒤에" (B), "한 주가 지나" (R)
decisions.reason: "여드레" is the native Korean count of eight days and keeps the Greek's inclusive reckoning at Literal; Balanced and Readable give the week the meaning decision explains.

source.text: ἔρχεται ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῶν θυρῶν κεκλεισμένων, καὶ ἔστη εἰς τὸ μέσον καὶ εἶπεν· Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν.

en.B: Though the doors were locked, Jesus came and stood among them and said, "Peace to you."
en.R: The doors were locked, but Jesus came and stood among them. He said, "Peace be with you."

sw.R: Milango ilikuwa imefungwa kwa kufuli, lakini Yesu alikuja, akasimama katikati yao. Akasema, "Amani iwe nanyi."

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu đến trong khi các cửa đã đóng kín, rồi đứng ở giữa và nói: "Bình an cho các con."
vi.B: Dù cửa đã khóa, Đức Giê-xu vẫn đến, đứng giữa họ và nói: "Bình an cho các con."
vi.R: Cửa đã khóa, nhưng Đức Giê-xu vẫn đến và đứng giữa họ. Ngài nói: "Bình an ở cùng các con."

ko.L: 문들이 닫혀 있는데 예수께서 오신다. 그리고 가운데 서시고 말씀하셨다. "평안이 너희에게 [있기를]."
ko.B: 문이 잠겨 있었는데도 예수께서 오셔서 그들 가운데 서시고 말씀하셨다. "너희에게 평안이 있기를 빈다."
ko.R: 문은 잠겨 있었다. 그런데 예수께서 오셔서 그들 가운데 서셨다. 그리고 말씀하셨다. "너희에게 평안이 있기를!"

decisions.choice: the doors having been shut: though the doors were shut
alternatives: after the doors had been shut, simply giving the time
decisions.reason: The phrase stands on its own beside the verb, and the context gives it the sense "although": the shut doors did not keep him out. As in 20:19, John does not say how he came in.

decisions.choice: Peace to you: the same greeting a third time
decisions.reason: Jesus greets them exactly as he did a week before (20:19, 21). The greeting carries the peace he promised (14:27), now offered to Thomas too.

decisions.choice: Though the doors were locked, Jesus came (B); The doors were locked, but (R)
alternatives: Jesus comes, the doors having been shut (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the sense "although" (meaning decision m1) and use the past tense (see 20:19 on the historic present). "Locked" and "Peace be with you" as in 20:19.

decisions.choice: historic present "đến" with no "đã" at Literal
decisions.reason: Vietnamese has no tense; Literal shows the Greek present by leaving out the past marker, as the style guide sets. Balanced and Readable read naturally as past in context.

source.text: εἶτα λέγει τῷ Θωμᾷ· Φέρε τὸν δάκτυλόν σου ὧδε καὶ ἴδε τὰς χεῖράς μου, καὶ φέρε τὴν χεῖρά σου καὶ βάλε εἰς τὴν πλευράν μου, καὶ μὴ γίνου ἄπιστος ἀλλὰ πιστός.

records.literal_gloss: Then he says to the Thomas, "Bring the finger of you here and see the hands of me, and bring the hand of you and put into the side of me, and not become unbelieving but believing."

en.L: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to Thomas, "Bring your finger here and see {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hands, and bring your hand and put [it] into {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} side, and do not be unbelieving, but believing."
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to Thomas, "Put your finger here; see {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hands. Bring your hand and put it into {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} side. Do not be unbelieving any longer, but believing."
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to Thomas, "Here, put your finger on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hands and look at them. Stretch out your hand and put it into {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} side. Do not refuse to believe any longer. Believe!"

fr.L: Ensuite {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit à Thomas : « Avance ton doigt ici et vois {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} mains, et avance ta main et mets-[la] dans {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} côté, et ne deviens pas incrédule, mais croyant. »
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit à Thomas : « Mets ton doigt ici ; regarde {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} mains. Avance ta main et mets-la dans {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} côté. Ne reste pas incrédule : deviens croyant. »
fr.R: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dit à Thomas : « Tiens, mets ton doigt sur {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} mains et regarde-les. Tends ta main et mets-la dans {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} côté. Ne refuse plus de croire. Crois ! »

sw.L: Kisha anamwambia Tomaso, "Kilete kidole chako hapa, uione mikono {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; na uulete mkono wako, uutie katika ubavu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}; wala usiwe mtu asiyeamini, bali mtu anayeamini."
sw.B: Kisha akamwambia Tomaso, "Weka kidole chako hapa; tazama mikono {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Lete mkono wako, uutie katika ubavu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. Acha kuwa mtu asiyeamini; uwe mtu anayeamini."
sw.R: Kisha akamwambia Tomaso, "Haya, weka kidole chako juu ya mikono {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, uitazame. Nyoosha mkono wako, uutie katika ubavu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}. Usiendelee kukataa kuamini. Amini!"

vi.L: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với Thô-ma: "Hãy đưa ngón tay con đến đây và xem tay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; hãy đưa bàn tay con ra và đặt vào sườn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; và đừng là người không tin, nhưng là người tin."
vi.B: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bảo Thô-ma: "Hãy đặt ngón tay con vào đây; hãy xem tay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Hãy đưa bàn tay con ra và đặt vào sườn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Đừng cứ mãi không tin, nhưng hãy tin."
vi.R: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với Thô-ma: "Này, hãy đặt ngón tay con lên tay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và nhìn xem. Hãy giơ bàn tay con ra và đặt vào sườn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Đừng từ chối tin nữa. Hãy tin đi!"

ko.L: 그러고 나서 도마에게 말씀하신다. "네 손가락을 이리 가져와 내 손을 보아라. 그리고 네 손을 가져와 내 옆구리에 넣어라. 그리고 믿지 않는 사람이 되지 말고 믿는 사람이 되어라."
ko.B: 그리고 도마에게 말씀하셨다. "네 손가락을 여기 대 보고 내 손을 보아라. 네 손을 내밀어 내 옆구리에 넣어 보아라. 더 이상 믿지 않는 사람으로 있지 말고 믿는 사람이 되어라."
ko.R: 그리고 도마에게 말씀하셨다. "자, 네 손가락을 여기 내 손에 대 보고 잘 보아라. 네 손을 뻗어 내 옆구리에 넣어 보아라. 이제 믿지 않으려고 버티지 말고 믿어라!"

decisions.choice: Jesus answers Thomas's demand point by point
decisions.reason: Thomas had named his finger, the hands, his hand and the side (20:25). Jesus offers each of these, though he was not there when Thomas spoke. He knows what is in people (1:47-48; 2:25). The text does not say that Thomas then touched him.

decisions.choice: unbelieving, believing: not believing and believing
alternatives: faithless and faithful, that is, disloyal and loyal
decisions.reason: The two words, ἄπιστος and πιστός, can mean "unfaithful" and "faithful". Here they belong to the same word family as "believe", and the context is about believing (20:25, 29, 31), so they mean refusing to believe and believing.

decisions.choice: do not be, do not become: do not go on as one who refuses to believe
decisions.reason: The verb means "become" or "be", in a present-tense command with "not". Jesus calls Thomas at the point of choosing not to settle into unbelief but to believe.

decisions.choice: Put your finger here (B); put your finger on my hands, Stretch out your hand (R); Do not be unbelieving any longer, but believing (B); Do not refuse to believe any longer. Believe! (R)
alternatives: Bring your finger here; Stop doubting
decisions.reason: The verb "bring" here means to move a hand or finger toward something; Balanced says "put" for the finger and keeps "bring" for the hand, and Readable says "put" and "stretch out" and joins the finger to the hands it is to touch. Balanced and Readable keep the word family of "believe" (meaning decision m2) rather than "doubt", and "any longer" carries the sense of m3.

decisions.choice: ne deviens pas incrédule, mais croyant (L); Ne reste pas incrédule : deviens croyant (B); Ne refuse plus de croire. Crois ! (R)
decisions.reason: The two adjectives are about believing (meaning decision m2), so French keeps "croyant" and "croire" rather than "douter", and "incrédule" is the plain word for one who will not believe. Literal keeps the verb "become"; Balanced's "Ne reste pas ... deviens" brings out the present command, a call not to settle into unbelief (m3), and Readable's "plus" does the same.

decisions.choice: mtu asiyeamini ... mtu anayeamini (L, B); Usiendelee kukataa kuamini. Amini! (R)
decisions.reason: The two Greek words belong to the family of "believe" (meaning decision m2), so every level uses "kuamini", the key term, rather than "mwaminifu" (faithful). Balanced says "Acha kuwa" (stop being) for the present command with "not" (m3).

decisions.choice: Jesus calls Thomas "con"
decisions.reason: Jesus addresses a single disciple as "con", matching "các con" for the group (style guide section 6).

decisions.choice: "믿지 않는 사람 ... 믿는 사람" (L, B); "믿지 않으려고 버티지 말고 믿어라" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek pair is built on the verb "believe", which John keeps at every level; "의심" (doubt) would make Thomas's fault hesitation rather than refusal, and "불신자" is a church label. Readable turns the pair into a plain command.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη Θωμᾶς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὁ κύριός μου καὶ ὁ θεός μου.

records.literal_gloss: Answered Thomas and said to him, "The Lord of me and the God of me."

en.B: Thomas answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "My Lord and my God!"
en.R: Thomas said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "My Lord and my God!"

fr.L: Thomas répondit et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Mon Seigneur et mon Dieu ! »
fr.B: Thomas {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondit : « Mon Seigneur et mon Dieu ! »
fr.R: Thomas {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a dit : « Mon Seigneur et mon Dieu ! »

sw.L: Tomaso akajibu, akamwambia, "Bwana wangu na Mungu wangu!"
sw.B: Tomaso akamjibu, "Bwana wangu na Mungu wangu!"
sw.R: Tomaso akamwambia, "Bwana wangu na Mungu wangu!"

vi.L: Thô-ma trả lời và nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Lạy Chúa của con và Đức Chúa Trời của con!"
vi.B: Thô-ma thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Lạy Chúa của con và Đức Chúa Trời của con!"
vi.R: Thô-ma thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Lạy Chúa của con và Đức Chúa Trời của con!"

ko.L: 도마가 대답하여 그분께 말씀드렸다. "나의 주님, 나의 하나님!"
ko.B: 도마가 예수께 대답했다. "나의 주님, 나의 하나님!"
ko.R: 도마가 예수께 말씀드렸다. "나의 주님, 나의 하나님!"

decisions.choice: My Lord and my God: Thomas confesses Jesus himself as Lord and God
alternatives: an exclamation of surprise addressed to God the Father
decisions.reason: Thomas "said to him": the words are spoken to Jesus. They are the highest confession in the Gospel and close the frame John opened at the start, "the Word was God" (1:1) and "the one and only God" who makes the Father known (1:18). The book that began by saying who the Word is ends with a disciple saying it to his face.

decisions.choice: the nominative with the article used as an address
alternatives: a statement: "(he is) my Lord and my God"
decisions.reason: Greek often uses the nominative with the article to address someone (for example Mark 14:36, "Abba, Father"). With "said to him", the words are a cry addressed to Jesus.

decisions.choice: Lord and God: the way Israel addressed its God
decisions.reason: The Psalms join the two words in calling on the God of Israel: "my God and my Lord" (Psalm 35:23). Thomas gives Jesus the names Israel gave to God.

decisions.choice: my: a personal confession
decisions.reason: Thomas does not only say who Jesus is; he says whose he is: "my" Lord, "my" God.

decisions.choice: My Lord and my God!
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the exact words, the climax of the book's confession. "My" is Thomas speaking of himself, so it takes no reader setting; "him" refers to Jesus and does.

decisions.choice: Bwana wangu na Mungu wangu!
decisions.reason: Every level keeps Thomas's exact words (meaning decision m1). "Wangu" is Thomas speaking of himself, so it takes no reader setting; the pronoun for Jesus is the object prefix -m- in the verb, which carries no span.

decisions.choice: "Lạy Chúa của con và Đức Chúa Trời của con!"
alternatives: "Lạy Chúa tôi và Đức Chúa Trời tôi!" (1926)
"Chúa của con, Đức Chúa Trời của con!"
decisions.reason: "Lạy" is the vocative of prayer and worship, fitting a confession addressed to Jesus; Thomas calls himself "con", the worshipper's word before God, rather than the plain "tôi".

decisions.choice: "나의 주님, 나의 하나님!" as an exclamation, with no sentence ending
decisions.reason: The Greek is a cry of address, not a statement; a verbless exclamation keeps that and needs no speech-level ending. "나의" is the fuller form of "my" and gives the confession its weight.

source.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ὅτι ἑώρακάς με πεπίστευκας;

records.literal_gloss: Says to him the Jesus, "Because you have seen me, you have believed?"

decisions.choice: a question (SBLGNT)
alternatives: a statement: "Because you have seen me, you have believed."
decisions.reason: The oldest manuscripts have no punctuation, and the words can be read either way. The SBLGNT prints a question. Either way Jesus accepts Thomas's belief and points beyond it to those who will believe without seeing.

decisions.choice: you have seen, you have believed: a sight that brought lasting belief

decisions.choice: Have you believed because ...? (B); Is it because ... that you believe? (R)

decisions.choice: blessed: in a good state in God's sight
decisions.reason: The word is the one in 13:17, the only other place John uses it, and in the beatitudes (Matthew 5:3-11). It declares people well off before God, whatever they feel.

decisions.choice: those who did not see and believed: those who come to believe without seeing
alternatives: the disciples, who believed before they saw
decisions.reason: The participles are aorist and describe the whole group of those who believe without seeing. They are those Jesus prayed for, who believe through the disciples' word (17:20), and the readers John writes for in the next verses (20:31). Jesus does not take back his acceptance of Thomas's belief.

decisions.choice: and: and yet
decisions.reason: The word "and" joins two things that do not usually go together, not seeing and believing, so it has the force "and yet".

decisions.choice: Blessed are those who have believed without having seen (B); God's blessing is on those who have not seen me and still believe (R)
alternatives: Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "blessed" as at 13:17; Readable names God as the one who blesses, as it does there. Balanced and Readable express "and yet" (meaning decision m3) in natural English, and Readable supplies "me", whom they have not seen.

decisions.choice: Bienheureux (L, B); Dieu bénit (R)
decisions.reason: The word declares people well off before God, not merely happy (meaning decision m1). French "heureux", the usual word in the Beatitudes, now says first of all "happy"; "bienheureux" keeps the sense of a blessing from God. Readable names God as the one who blesses, as the English Readable does. 13:17 uses the same word; a reviewer should settle "bienheureux" or "heureux" for both together.

decisions.choice: Heri (L, B); Baraka ya Mungu iko juu ya (R)
decisions.reason: The same word as at 13:17, the only other place John uses it (meaning decision m1). "Heri" is the Swahili word for this declaration and the form of the beatitudes; at 13:17 Balanced needed a verb for the conditional ("mmebarikiwa"), but here the declaration stands on its own. Readable names God as the one who blesses, as at 13:17.

decisions.choice: "Phước [cho]"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese needs "cho" to say whom the blessing is on; the Greek has a bare adjective.

decisions.choice: "복되다" (L, B); "하나님의 복이 있다" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word describes a good standing in God's sight, not a feeling; "행복하다" would make it an emotion. Readable names God as the giver, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: signs: deeds that point to who Jesus is
decisions.reason: "Signs" is John's word for the deeds of Jesus that show his glory and lead people to believe (2:11; 12:37). John has told a selection of them; there were many more (21:25).

decisions.choice: So then ... but these: a contrast with the next sentence
decisions.reason: The opening words prepare for the contrast in 20:31: many signs are not written, but these are written for a purpose. The sentence looks back over the whole book.

decisions.choice: in the presence of the disciples: done before witnesses
decisions.reason: The disciples saw the signs and can testify to them, because they have been with Jesus from the beginning (15:27). The book rests on their witness (19:35; 21:24).

decisions.choice: while the disciples looked on (B); while his disciples were watching (R); written down (B)
alternatives: in the presence of the disciples
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the phrase into everyday words that keep the idea of witnesses (meaning decision m3). Readable says "his disciples" and makes two sentences.

decisions.choice: "dấu lạ" for "sign"
decisions.reason: The book-wide key term from the style guide: a deed that points beyond itself, never "phép lạ".

decisions.choice: so that you may believe, present tense (SBLGNT)
alternatives: πιστεύσητε, aorist: "so that you may come to believe"
decisions.reason: Some of the oldest manuscripts, including Codex Vaticanus and the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus, and probably the papyrus P66, have the present tense, which can mean "continue to believe". Many others, including Codex Alexandrinus and most later manuscripts, have the aorist, which can mean "come to believe". The difference bears on whether the book was written mainly to strengthen believers or to bring others to believe. Yet tenses in purpose clauses like this do not draw a sharp line, and John uses both for both purposes (compare 19:35; 11:15), so the book can serve both. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Christ, the Son of God: a title, the Messiah, with its fullest meaning
decisions.reason: "The Christ" is the anointed king Israel was waiting for (1:41; 4:25-26; 7:41-42). Martha confessed Jesus in the same words: "you are the Christ, the Son of God" (11:27). John fills "Son of God" with the meaning the whole book has given it (1:18; 5:18; 10:30-36; 20:28).

decisions.choice: life: eternal life, the life of God given now
decisions.reason: "Life" here is the eternal life John speaks of throughout (3:15-16; 5:24; 10:10; 17:3): life with God that begins when a person believes and does not end.

decisions.choice: in his name: through him, through who he is
decisions.reason: A name stands for the person. Life "in his name" is life that comes through Jesus and belongs to those joined to him, as "believe in his name" means to believe in him (1:12; 3:18).

decisions.choice: these: the signs written in this book
decisions.reason: "These" picks up the signs of 20:30 that are written, in contrast to the many that are not. The book as a whole was written for this purpose.

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: "The Christ" is a title here, so every level writes "the" before it (see the book's terms); the reader may choose "Messiah".

decisions.choice: by believing have life (B); these signs; And when you believe, you will have life through him (R)
alternatives: believing, you may have life in his name (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced renders the participle "by believing", which keeps the link between believing and having life. Readable names "these" as the signs (meaning decision m5) and says "through him" for "in his name" (m4). "You may believe" is kept at Balanced so that the meaning of the tense stays as open as the Greek (m1).

decisions.choice: le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}
decisions.reason: A title with the article (meaning decision m2), so every level writes "le" outside the span, as in 1:20.

decisions.choice: afin que vous croyiez / pour que vous croyiez
alternatives: afin que vous continuiez à croire
afin que vous en veniez à croire
decisions.reason: The French present subjunctive does not mark the difference between the Greek present and aorist, so "croyiez" leaves open, as the Greek text and its variant do, whether readers are to go on believing or to come to believe (meaning decision m1). Readable keeps it too.

decisions.choice: Yesu ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}
decisions.reason: Swahili has no article to show that "the Christ" is a title. "Ndiye" (he is the one) does that, as "siye" does at 1:20 and "ndiwe" at 11:27, and both setting options read naturally after it. "Hizi" agrees with "ishara" (signs), which is what "these" refers to (meaning decision m5).

decisions.choice: ili mwamini ... uzima
decisions.reason: "Uzima" is life itself, the word in "uzima wa milele", which is the life meant here (meaning decision m3); "maisha" would suggest a lifetime or daily living. The Swahili subjunctive "ili mwamini" does not mark the difference between coming to believe and going on believing, so the question of the tense (m1) stays as open as in the English.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}
decisions.reason: The style guide's christos span for "the Christ" as a title.

decisions.choice: "anh chị em" for the readers ("you" plural)
decisions.reason: The narrator addresses the readers directly; Vietnamese must choose a relation, and "anh chị em" is the warm, inclusive form used in churches. Plain text, not a gender span, since the Greek has no "brothers" here.

decisions.choice: the readers addressed as "여러분" (B, R); "너희" (L)
decisions.reason: Here the narrator turns to the readers. "너희" is the plain plural you that Jesus uses to his disciples, but from a writer to his readers modern Korean says "여러분"; Literal keeps the plain pronoun.

decisions.choice: {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} with no word for "the", followed by "이시며" / "이시고"
decisions.reason: Korean has no article, and the predicate already reads as a title; the honorific copula fits both alternatives of the setting.
